answer: In PoA, each identity escrows bonded collateral, while signed histories expose coordinated equivocation. When k identities act together, the joint penalty scales quadratically, O(k^2), rather than linearly; detection then applies an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s capital loss, and asymmetric depreciation destroys residual stake over time. A vine marker, raven signature, or sable alias cannot conceal shared control.
